title: Patterns of Motion
seo_title: Grade 3 Motion Worksheets: Patterns of Motion and Predicting with Data
standard_text: Make observations and/or measurements of an object’s motion to provide evidence that a pattern can be used to predict future motion.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on patterns of motion (NGSS 3-PS2-2): swings and pendulums, back and forth and circular motion, steady motion tables and predicting future motion. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Patterns of motion help us predict what comes next.
key_sub: A swing goes back and forth in a regular pattern. If we measure it, we can predict where it will be.
body_html:
How to think about it

Many objects move in patterns that repeat: a swing goes back and forth, a merry-go-round goes around in a circle, a yo-yo goes up and down.

When we observe and measure motion (with a stopwatch and a meter stick), we can find the pattern and predict what will happen next.

Example

A car moves 15 cm each second: 0, 15, 30, 45 cm. Where will it be at 4 seconds?

It adds 15 cm each second.

45 + 15 = 60

Answer: 60 cm

Example

A swing goes back and forth 6 times in 10 seconds. How many times in 20 seconds?

20 seconds is 2 × 10 seconds.

2 × 6 = 12

Answer: 12 times

Common mistakes

  • Thinking motion cannot be predicted. Repeating patterns can be predicted.
  • Adding the wrong amount when the object moves the same distance each second.
  • Thinking a swing keeps going forever. Friction slowly stops it.

faq.q: What is a pattern of motion?
faq.a: It is a way of moving that repeats, like a swing going back and forth or a merry-go-round turning in circles.

faq.q: How can you predict future motion?
faq.a: Measure the motion, find the pattern, and use it to say what will happen next.

faq.q: Why does a swing stop if no one pushes it?
faq.a: Friction and the air slow it down a little on each swing.
